title: Gieseker stability and closedness of the ten-canonical locus
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], $g\geq2$, $d=20(g-1)$, $r=19(g-1)$ and $P(m)=dm+1-g$. Let $Z=\operatorname{Hilb}^{P}(\mathbf P^{r-1}_k)$ be the projective Hilbert scheme $H_P$ of [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] for $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $E=\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$, and let $J\subset Z$ be the locally closed subscheme of [lem-sfb-ten-canonical-hilbert-parameter], its locus of complete ten-canonical embeddings of unpointed stable genus-$g$ curves: fibrewise the curve is stable in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and its hyperplane line is the tenth tensor power of its dualizing line, with base-line twists permitted in families. Let $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$ act by changing projective coordinates. For all sufficiently large integers $m$ (depending on $g$), the Hilbert embedding sends an embedded curve to the quotient $\operatorname{Sym}^m(k^r)\twoheadrightarrow H^0(C,\mathcal O_C(m))$ of dimension $P(m)$, followed by the Pluecker embedding of this quotient Grassmannian. A positive tensor power $A$ of its hyperplane line has a $G$-linearization, meaning an action lifting the $G$-action to the line and linear on each fibre. For this linearization, $J\subset Z^s(A)$ and $J\hookrightarrow Z^{ss}(A)$ is a closed immersion. A geometric point is semistable if some invariant section of a positive power of $A$ does not vanish there, and is stable if, in addition, its orbit is closed in the semistable locus and its stabilizer has dimension zero. These assertions hold in every characteristic, with no invertibility assumption on $r$ or on orders of automorphism groups.

source.place: Section 3.3 Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, printed pp.16--17, with canonical multiple nu=10 (nu>=5 suffices); the Gieseker construction. Positive tensor power removes the central scalar action in passing from SL_r to PGL_r. Local PDF WANTED; author exposition read online.

proof.text: Choose $m$ above all three uniform Hilbert, smooth-stability and potential-stability bounds; $d>9(g-1)$ and $d\geq2g+1$. The Hilbert-Pluecker theorem gives the stated quotient, embedding and $A=\Lambda_m^{\otimes r}$ with its descended $G$-linearization; its comparison preserves both stability loci even if $\operatorname{char}k\mid r$.

source.place: Section 2.1 and Section 3.3, choice of nu=10 before Proposition 10

proof.text: For any trait in $Z^{ss}$ generically in $J$, nodal preparation gives a connected nodal family and a complete special embedding of genus $g$, with generically trivial $T=L\otimes\omega^{-10}$ and the balanced degree bound. The balanced-limit lemma makes this special curve stable with $L_C\simeq\omega_C^{10}$; the parameter theorem puts its point in $J$.

source.place: Section 3.3, Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, printed pp.16--17; agent expansion, local PDF WANTED, source read online

proof.text: Put $J^{ss}=J\cap Z^{ss}$. Its immersion is of finite type in a Noetherian scheme. A boundary point would give a DVR with generic lift into $J^{ss}$, contrary to step 2. Its image is closed, so the immersion is closed.

proof.text: For any geometric $z\in J$, framed smoothing gives $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[[t]]\to J$ with special point $z$ and smooth generic curve. Smooth high-degree stability and step 1 make its generic Hilbert point stable.

source.place: Section 3.3, Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, printed pp.16--17; agent expansion, local PDF WANTED, source read online

proof.text: Semistable replacement gives a dominating DVR $R\to R'$, $h\in G(K')$ and $\beta:\operatorname{Spec}R'\to Z^{ss}$ with $\beta_{K'}=h\alpha_{K'}$. As $J$ is $G$-invariant, its generic point is in $J^{ss}$, and its generic curve is isomorphic to that of $\mathcal C_{R'}$. The closed ideal of $J^{ss}$ maps to zero in $K'=\operatorname{Frac}(R')$, hence in $R'$, so $\beta$ factors through $J^{ss}$ and supplies a second stable family $\mathcal C'$.

source.place: Section 3.3, Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, printed pp.16--17; agent expansion, local PDF WANTED, source read online

proof.text: The generic isomorphism identifies the graded $R'$-algebras $\bigoplus_{a\geq0}H^0(\mathcal C_{R'},\omega^{\otimes a})$ and $\bigoplus_{a\geq0}H^0(\mathcal C',\omega^{\otimes a})$: lattice restriction is injective and the identifications respect products. Stable component degrees are positive, so canonical reconstruction identifies both families with the Proj of that algebra. Their special curves are isomorphic; this induces an isomorphism of their ten-canonical section spaces, so the complete ten-canonical frames put their points in one $G$-orbit. As $Z^{ss}$ is $G$-invariant, $z$ is semistable. Field-extension compatibility gives $J\subset Z^{ss}$ and step 3 gives its closed immersion.

source.place: Section 3.3, Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, printed pp.16--17; agent expansion, local PDF WANTED, source read online

proof.text: Base change to an algebraically closed $\Omega\supseteq k$; the stability loci commute with this. The frame description identifies each stabilizer with its curve automorphism scheme. Isom-finiteness over the finite-type base $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ makes it finite. An orbit boundary in the closed invariant $J\subset Z^{ss}$ would have smaller dimension, whereas all its orbits have dimension $\dim G$. Hence every orbit is closed and every $z\in J$ is stable.
